colour_meaning: Review: one strong sign of risk, or two weaker ones.

items.label: Very fast award after bid opening
items.detail: Award made 7 days after the bid deadline (past road contracts awarded this fast had about twice the odds of termination)

items.label: Re-tendered
items.detail: 1 earlier PhilGEPS notice(s) for this contract failed or were cancelled (2 notices in all).

items.label: Regional cost factor
items.detail: Prices for similar works in Region IX (Zamboanga Peninsula) run ×0.92 the national median; adjusted for the region: ₱59.0M per km vs national 95th percentile ₱75.5M.

items.label: High earlier termination rate
items.detail: ALRAF CONST. AND ENTERPRISES INC. (FORMERLY:ALRAF CONSTRUCTION & ENTERPRISES): 11% of its finished DPWH contracts were terminated (5%+ went with about 4x the odds of termination; not yet confirmed on recent years)

items.label: Road contracts from other agencies (PhilGEPS)
items.detail: Grace Construction Corporation also won 3 road contract(s) worth ₱206.9M from 1 other procuring entity (2022–2025), e.g. City Of Oroquieta, Misamis Occidental. PhilGEPS awards record no outcome, so this is not scored.

families.name: Contractor ownership, affiliation and bidding networks

items.label: Political dynasties in the province (Ateneo dataset)
items.detail: 22% of Zamboanga Sibugay's elected local positions were held by fat-dynastic officials after the 2025 election (16% in 2001); median province 28%; largest clan: Ruste (1.7% of positions); family poverty incidence 37% (2012).

items.label: Potential dynasts after the 2025 election (House CPBRD inventory)
items.detail: 36% of elected officials in the province have potential dynastic links (national average 54.5%; broader name matching than the Ateneo measure).

items.label: Political families in the province
items.detail: 0 of 1 elected officials in Zamboanga Sibugay (2025-2028) have a relative also in elective office (0%; national median 25%).

items.label: Weak: most of the winner's recent CPES evaluations are behind schedule
items.detail: Grace Construction Corporation: of 13 CPES evaluation(s) of its other DPWH contracts in the last 3 years, 8 (62%) were behind schedule. Worst, on 2024-06-28: 9.8% negative slippage during construction (CPES scored schedule 0.052 of 0.15) (contract 24KD0034).

items.label: Winner's other on-going roads
items.detail: Grace Construction Corporation has 3 on-going DPWH road(s) possibly stalled and 5 far behind schedule (weekly stage-3 list; DPWH progress data can lag).

assessment.derivation: 0 strong + 2 weak signal(s) → Medium priority (1 strong, or 2 weak) → Yellow.

steps.title: Confirm the basic facts on the official DPWH page
sub: Budget, location, status, dates and bidders match this page.

steps.title: Open the bid documents
sub: Look for the quantities, a Bill of Quantities and technical specifications.

steps.title: Read Claude's check and confirm its points against the sources
Verify the risk: Procurement competition and bidding patterns
sub: Compare the bid-opening date with the Notice of Award date.
Ask whether post-qualification (checking the winner's documents and capacity) could be done that fast.

steps.title: Verify the risk: Implementation delays and performance anomalies
sub: Compare DPWH's reported progress with citizen reports, Bisto.ph inspections and satellite images.

If CPES is cited: open the DPWH quarterly CPES report for that date and confirm the contract, the slippage and the scores. A CPES rating is the agency's own evaluation; ask the district office for the evaluation sheet and the catch-up programme.

steps.title: Check site and field evidence
sub: Check progress on site: geotagged photos (from a monitor, a TPM civil-society partner or Bisto.ph), citizen reports on the DPWH portal, and DPWH's reported progress against the planned dates.

steps.title: Write down what you found and keep the documents you relied on
sub: Screenshots, Bill of Quantities pages, photos or letters: attach them with your decision.
